title: Ben Johnson on preparing for Packers | Press Conference
headline: Tyson Bagent is expected to start again at Lambeau, with Ben Johnson pushing him to take more deep shots and Rome Odunze set to see more early targets.
summary: Johnson opened by calling Green Bay a good team with a strong special teams unit, fast defenders, and a dangerous Packers offense led by Jordan Love, and said the road game will be a big challenge. He said the Packers' safeties fly around and will disguise coverages, so Bagent must keep his eyes disciplined and receivers must be precise in their routes. He praised Bagent's processing and said Bagent has handled pre-snap changes for the past year and a half, but he wants him to pull the trigger on second-level throws the team has been missing. Johnson said the crowd and cadence will be a test, and the team has used chaos in practice to prepare for it. He framed Bagent's next step as improving from his first start to his next, and said the team is still in a improvement phase after four weeks. On the skill players, he said Odunze and others needed more touches early and that Odunze's confidence is not the issue. Johnson said Swift's two fumbles are uncharacteristic, that last week's was egregious, and that ball security must tighten. He said Theo Benedet played solidly in the run game and will keep improving, and that Ozzy Trapilo is getting closer each week with a decision on the three returning players to be made at the end of the week. He called Jonah Jackson the team's top-graded offensive lineman and said his demeanor carries weight. Practice today will be padded but managed to balance reps after a heavy game workload.

injuries.detail: Getting closer each week after being on the 53; a decision on whether he and two other returning players are active will come at the end of the week.

signals.claim: Bagent will start again at Green Bay and is expected to take more shots downfield.
signals.note: Johnson is treating Bagent as the starter again and encouraging him to be more aggressive, which could lift his passing volume and upside.

signals.note: Johnson said he wants to get Odunze the ball earlier, which could boost his volume and big-play chances.

topics.detail: Johnson said Green Bay has new special teams and defensive schemes, a fast secondary, a new Mike linebacker who is instinctive, and a strong front, and said Packers coordinator Gannon does a great job.
The team will have a padded practice to work on technique, with reps managed after a heavy workload in the last game, when the offense ran 89 plays.

There is one open roster spot, and decisions on returning players will be made at the end of the week. A player named Davenport retired after one game, which the coach called unexpected; the name is not on the roster provided.
Johnson said the team has used varying cadences and chaos in practice so that the crowd and pre-snap noise will not disrupt the offense, which is key for a road game at Lambeau.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Taking Over the Defense & Tank Dell’s Return
headline: M.J. Stewart is healthy and expected to play Sunday, while Tank Dell took his first practice back with no set return timeline.
summary: Ryans said the Titans have been in close games, have played tough opponents, and have a strong quarterback, two good running backs, an aggressive defense, and a good special teams unit. On Tank Dell, he said Dell looked great in his first practice back, running routes and plays, and that the team will ease him into team reps without a hard deadline. He said Kayden McDonald and two other players also returned to practice this week and will be progressed individually. M.J. Stewart is healthy, has practiced well the past couple of weeks, and will be ready Sunday. On the defense, Ryans acknowledged the lack of interceptions, said the team has been close to turnovers and needs to keep attacking the ball, and said the team must improve its communication. He announced that he will take over defensive play-calling from Matt Burke to streamline communication and spark change. He said Burke has done a good job and that the defense is not being overhauled. On the run game, he said the offensive line must sustain blocks better to handle Jeffrey Simmons and the Titans' interior pressure. He also described his close friendship with Robert Saleh and called the game a must-win for both AFC South teams.

title: Jim Harbaugh on the Rookie Offensive Linemen Stepping Up
headline: Harbaugh: Rookie OL earning expanded roles, Charlie Kolar back early from surgery, and Rashawn Slater, Joe Alt, Trevor Penning, Derwin James, and Donte Jackson won't practice Wednesday.
summary: Harbaugh opened with an injury update: Rashawn Slater, Joe Alt, Trevor Penning, Derwin James, and Donte Jackson will not practice, Khalil Mack is resting, and Brenen Thompson and Ladd McConkey will be at practice with their workload still unclear. He said Thompson is working through something. He was encouraged by the returns of Charlie Kolar, who had surgery about two weeks ago and already did some work last week, and Scott Matlock and Branson Taylor. He added that Daniel Brunskill was brought in and praised his versatility. On the rookie offensive linemen, Harbaugh said confidence is earned rather than given, and that they proved themselves in a game last weekend and showed a focused, ready-for-the-challenge demeanor. He compared it to his own days as a veteran quarterback stepping into the huddle with young linemen. He said Travis Burke split time at tight end and tackle, and that he wants Burke focused solely on tackle this week. Looking ahead to Denver, Harbaugh praised Sean Payton's staff for its schematic approach, noting the Broncos will mix man and zone, match well, and have an excellent, well-coordinated, talented pass rush and defensive line. He also praised Bo Nix's mobility and playmaking.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 7, 2026
headline: Dameon Pierce steps up as the next back with Tank Bigsby down, and Markel Bell takes over as starting right tackle after Lane Johnson's retirement.
summary: Sirianni said he will miss Lane Johnson and that the relationship will last beyond his playing career. He praised Markel Bell's handling of the week's circumstances and said he is excited for Bell's growth this season after a year learning from Johnson. Sirianni described the team reset as a focus on the keys to beating a very good opponent, plus a message to stay together after a two-game losing streak. He framed the injuries and roster losses as life in the NFL that the team can't control, stressing practice preparation and effort as the controllable pieces. On defensive snaps, he said the defense's load depends on how long the offense stays on the field and that the team will manage it during the week. He said Pierce, who was elevated to the active roster, is a good back and that he is excited for the opportunity with Bigsby down. He also said the team is early in the season and will find what it does best, pointing to the 2024 season as an example of recovering from a similar start.

injuries.detail: Sirianni said Bigsby is down right now and that the team is bummed, but did not give a specific injury or timeline.

signals.claim: Pierce is the next running back up and steps into a lead role while Bigsby is down
signals.note: With Bigsby sidelined, Pierce becomes the primary backup-turned-lead option, which raises his touch floor for fantasy.
signals.quote: we got a really good back and you guys saw him run the football

signals.claim: Bell is the starting right tackle this year and will have a chance to grow
signals.note: Bell's new starting role is an offensive line development; it matters more for the Eagles' offensive line than for individual fantasy production.
signals.quote: I'm really excited for markel's opportunity

signals.claim: Bigsby is currently down and unavailable at this time
signals.note: A current absence removes Bigsby from the backfield picture until the team gives a clearer update.
signals.quote: Obviously bummed about the other guy you know about tank.

topics.detail: Sirianni said Johnson is retiring after this season and that the team feels good about the offensive tackle room. He was emotional about the relationship and said business continues as usual.
The team reviewed the keys to the game and emphasized staying together after a two-game losing streak. Sirianni described adversity as a source of growth.
Sirianni said the defense's high snap count late in the game is best handled by the offense staying on the field and finishing drives. The team will manage practice workloads during the week.
Sirianni said line cohesion comes from walk-through reps, practice reps, and meeting time, and that the team will work on it. He said the team can't control injuries but controls preparation.
Sirianni said he still has conviction in the offense being installed and pointed to the 2024 season, when the team made adjustments after a similar start and got on a roll.
